name: Paracetamol
commonUses: Relief of mild to moderate pain (headache, body ache, toothache, sore throat) and reduction of fever.
safetyGuide: Take with or without food. Do not exceed the maximum daily allowance stated on the approved product label. Avoid combining with multiple paracetamol-containing cough, cold, or sinus medications to prevent accidental liver toxicity.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Generally considered safe for short-term use during pregnancy and breastfeeding when taken at recommended therapeutic levels. Always consult a healthcare professional for persistent fever.
childrenWarning: For children, never guess or give adult formulations. Use age-appropriate pediatric drops, syrups, or suppositories measured with a calibrated oral syringe or measuring spoon. Consult a pediatrician.
emergencyWarning: In case of suspected overdose or taking excessive quantities, seek immediate emergency hospital care. Paracetamol overdose requires prompt medical antidote (N-acetylcysteine) intervention.
storage: Store below 30°C in a dry place protected from heat and moisture. Keep out of reach of children.

name: Ibuprofen
commonUses: Reduces inflammatory pain, joint stiffness, dental pain, menstrual cramps, and high fever.
safetyGuide: Always take with or immediately after meals with plenty of water to protect the stomach lining. Avoid taking if you have active stomach ulcers, severe kidney disease, or bleeding disorders.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Avoid use during the third trimester of pregnancy as it can cause fetal heart and kidney complications. Use during early pregnancy or breastfeeding only if specifically prescribed by a physician.
childrenWarning: Do not give to dehydrated children or infants under 6 months without direct pediatric guidance. Always use pediatric formulation with calibrated measuring syringe.
emergencyWarning: Seek emergency medical care immediately if you notice vomiting blood, black tarry stools, sudden chest pain, severe stomach cramps, or allergic facial swelling.
storage: Store in a dry location below 25°C protected from light.

name: Naproxen
commonUses: Long-lasting relief from osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, acute gout, musculoskeletal pain, and severe dysmenorrhea.
safetyGuide: Take with meals or milk. Often co-prescribed with a gastro-protective medicine (such as a PPI) in patients at risk of gastritis. Do not combine with other NSAIDs or aspirin.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Contraindicated in the third trimester of pregnancy. Consult a registered physician before using in early pregnancy or while nursing.
childrenWarning: Not recommended for young children unless specifically prescribed by a pediatric specialist for conditions like juvenile arthritis.
emergencyWarning: Seek immediate emergency help if you experience signs of gastrointestinal bleeding (dark stools, severe heartburn), sudden shortness of breath, or skin peeling.
storage: Store below 25°C in original blister packaging.

name: Tramadol
commonUses: Management of moderate to moderately severe acute or chronic post-surgical and injury pain.
safetyGuide: Controlled prescription medicine. Strictly follow physician instructions. May cause drowsiness, dizziness, or dependence with extended use. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Contraindicated during pregnancy and lactation due to the risk of neonatal respiratory depression and withdrawal symptoms.
childrenWarning: Strictly contraindicated in children under 12 years of age and in adolescents after tonsillectomy/adenoidectomy due to life-threatening breathing risks.
emergencyWarning: Seek emergency medical intervention immediately in case of severe drowsiness, slow/shallow breathing, seizures, confusion, or loss of consciousness.
storage: Store securely below 30°C in a locked cabinet out of reach of children and unauthorized individuals.

name: Ketorolac
commonUses: Short-term management of moderate to severe acute post-operative or post-traumatic pain.
safetyGuide: Maximum combined duration of treatment (oral + injection) must not exceed 5 consecutive days due to significant risk of peptic ulceration and kidney impairment.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Contraindicated during pregnancy, labor, delivery, and lactation.
childrenWarning: Not recommended for pediatric use outside controlled inpatient pediatric surgical settings under specialist supervision.
emergencyWarning: Emergency medical attention is required if there is sudden fluid retention, severe stomach pain, gastrointestinal bleeding, or severe allergic reaction.
storage: Store protected from light and heat below 25°C.

name: Aceclofenac
commonUses: Relief of pain and inflammation in osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, and dental pain.
safetyGuide: Take with or after food. Swallow tablets whole with plenty of liquid. Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration necessary.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Should not be administered during pregnancy (especially third trimester) or while breastfeeding unless explicitly advised by a doctor.
childrenWarning: Safety and efficacy have not been established in children. Not recommended for pediatric use.
emergencyWarning: Discontinue immediately and seek medical care if experiencing severe skin rashes, gastrointestinal bleeding, or difficulty breathing.
storage: Store in a dry place below 30°C.

name: Diclofenac
commonUses: Relief of inflammatory pain from acute musculoskeletal trauma, arthritis, migraine, and post-operative dental procedures.
safetyGuide: Take after meals. Patients with existing cardiovascular disease, uncontrolled hypertension, or renal impairment should use with strict caution under doctor supervision.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Contraindicated during the third trimester of pregnancy. Avoid use during early pregnancy and lactation unless deemed essential by a specialist.
childrenWarning: Use only pediatric-specific formulations when strictly prescribed by a pediatrician.
emergencyWarning: Seek urgent hospital evaluation if chest pain, shortness of breath, sudden weakness, or black stools occur.
storage: Store below 25°C in moisture-resistant blisters.

name: Aspirin
commonUses: Low-dose (75mg/100mg) for cardiovascular/stroke prevention; higher doses for acute pain and inflammation.
safetyGuide: Take low-dose gastro-resistant tablets with food. Do not stop cardioprotective aspirin therapy without consulting your cardiologist.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: High doses contraindicated in pregnancy. Low-dose aspirin may only be used during pregnancy if prescribed by an obstetrician for preeclampsia prophylaxis.
childrenWarning: STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED in children and adolescents under 16 years with viral infections (influenza, chickenpox) due to the risk of fatal Reye's syndrome.
emergencyWarning: Seek urgent emergency medical care for unexplained bruising, coffee-ground vomiting, ringing in ears (tinnitus), or severe dizziness.
storage: Store below 25°C in a tightly closed container protected from humidity.

name: Omeprazole
commonUses: Suppresses stomach gastric acid secretion to treat peptic ulcers, gastritis, GERD, gas, and heartburn.
safetyGuide: Best taken 30 to 60 minutes before the first meal of the day. Swallow capsules whole with water; do not crush or chew beads inside.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Can be used during pregnancy and lactation when clinically indicated and approved by a physician.
childrenWarning: Pediatric use requires specific diagnosis and weight-adjusted dosing by a licensed pediatrician.
emergencyWarning: Seek medical evaluation if experiencing persistent difficulty swallowing, unintentional weight loss, or vomiting blood.
storage: Store below 25°C in a dry place protected from moisture.

name: Esomeprazole
commonUses: Treatment of acid reflux disease (GERD), erosive esophagitis, Zollinger-Ellison syndrome, and prevention of NSAID-induced ulcers.
safetyGuide: Take 30-60 minutes before breakfast. Long-term continuous use without medical supervision should be reviewed with a doctor to monitor magnesium and bone health.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Consult a healthcare provider before using during pregnancy or breastfeeding.
childrenWarning: Safety in young children should be determined and supervised by a pediatrician.
emergencyWarning: Get emergency medical care if you experience severe watery diarrhea, muscle spasms, or irregular heartbeat.
storage: Store below 30°C in moisture-proof packaging.

name: Pantoprazole
commonUses: Management of acute and chronic gastroesophageal reflux, gastric hypersecretion, gas discomfort, and peptic ulcer healing.
safetyGuide: Take once daily in the morning before food. Tablets are enteric-coated and should not be split or crushed.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Use only if clearly needed and advised by a registered physician.
childrenWarning: Not routinely recommended for children under 5 years unless prescribed by a pediatric gastroenterologist.
emergencyWarning: Seek prompt medical care for sudden severe allergic reactions, swelling, or persistent diarrhea.
storage: Store below 25°C protected from light and moisture.

name: Rabeprazole
commonUses: Rapid suppression of stomach acid for healing active duodenal ulcers, gastric ulcers, and GERD symptoms.
safetyGuide: Take in the morning before breakfast with a glass of water. Do not chew or crush enteric-coated tablets.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Avoid use during pregnancy and lactation unless approved by an obstetrician.
childrenWarning: Not recommended for children under 12 years of age without specialist prescription.
emergencyWarning: Contact a doctor if symptoms persist after 2 weeks or if dark stools and severe abdominal pain occur.
storage: Store in a cool, dry place below 25°C.

name: Famotidine
commonUses: Relief and prevention of heartburn, acid indigestion, sour stomach, and nocturnal acid breakthrough.
safetyGuide: Can be taken before meals or at bedtime to prevent nighttime acid symptoms. Dose adjustment is necessary in patients with moderate to severe renal impairment.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Generally safe when indicated, but physician consultation is recommended prior to use.
childrenWarning: Pediatric dosage should be guided by a doctor according to body weight.
emergencyWarning: Seek emergency medical help if you experience signs of severe allergic reaction, confusion, or heart palpitations.
storage: Store below 30°C in a dry location.

name: Domperidone
commonUses: Relief of nausea, vomiting, feeling of fullness, gas, upper abdominal bloating, and delayed gastric emptying.
safetyGuide: Take 15-30 minutes before meals. Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration (typically not exceeding 7 days) due to cardiac considerations.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Use during pregnancy only if benefits outweigh risks. Small amounts pass into breast milk; use under physician supervision.
childrenWarning: Administer to children only under pediatric prescription with strict weight-based measuring.
emergencyWarning: Seek immediate emergency attention if dizziness, fainting, or irregular heartbeat occurs.
storage: Store below 25°C protected from moisture.

name: Ondansetron
commonUses: Prevention and treatment of nausea and vomiting induced by chemotherapy, radiation, gastroenteritis, or surgical procedures.
safetyGuide: Can be taken with or without food. Dissolving tablets (ODT) should be placed on the tongue and allowed to dissolve before swallowing.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Consult your obstetrician before taking for hyperemesis gravidarum or pregnancy nausea.
childrenWarning: Safe in children when prescribed by a pediatrician based on body weight or body surface area.
emergencyWarning: Seek urgent medical care if you experience chest pain, severe dizziness, irregular heart rhythm, or vision changes.
storage: Store below 30°C away from excessive heat and direct sunlight.

name: Hyoscine Butylbromide
commonUses: Relief of painful smooth-muscle spasms of the gastrointestinal, biliary, and urinary tracts (e.g. stomach colic, menstrual cramps).
safetyGuide: Take with water as needed for acute spasmodic pain. Avoid in patients with untreated glaucoma, enlarged prostate, or bowel obstruction.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Avoid during pregnancy unless prescribed. Consult a physician before breastfeeding.
childrenWarning: Children over 6 years should only use under healthcare guidance. Not recommended for infants.
emergencyWarning: Seek emergency care if severe painful eye redness, urinary retention, or rapid heart rate occurs.
storage: Store in a cool dry place below 30°C.

name: Antacid (Magaldrate + Simethicone)
commonUses: Rapid relief from hyperacidity, stomach gas, gas bloating, heartburn, sour stomach, and dyspepsia.
safetyGuide: Take 20 to 60 minutes after meals and before bedtime. Shake suspension well before use. Chewable tablets must be chewed thoroughly before swallowing.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Generally safe for occasional short-term relief during pregnancy. Avoid excessive regular use without medical advice.
childrenWarning: Not recommended for infants or very young children without explicit doctor advice.
emergencyWarning: Consult a physician if heartburn symptoms do not improve after 7 consecutive days of self-treatment.
storage: Store below 30°C away from frost and direct sunlight.

name: Cetirizine
commonUses: Relief of allergic symptoms such as sneezing, runny nose, watery eyes, itching, dust allergy, and chronic hives (urticaria).
safetyGuide: Usually taken once daily in the evening. May cause mild drowsiness in some individuals; use care when driving or operating equipment.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Consult a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy or lactation.
childrenWarning: Pediatric syrups or drops should be used for children with precise calibrated measuring spoons.
emergencyWarning: Seek emergency medical care immediately for severe allergic reactions (swelling of throat, lips, or breathing difficulty).
storage: Store below 30°C in a dry place.

name: Levocetirizine
commonUses: Relief of seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis, allergy flare-ups, and chronic idiopathic urticaria.
safetyGuide: Take once daily in the evening with or without food. Avoid taking concurrently with excessive alcohol or sedatives.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Consult your doctor before taking during pregnancy or breastfeeding.
childrenWarning: Safety in infants under 6 months has not been established. Use pediatric syrup under medical supervision.
emergencyWarning: Immediate emergency care required if anaphylactic symptoms (wheezing, facial swelling) develop.
storage: Store in a dry location below 25°C.

name: Fexofenadine
commonUses: Relief of seasonal allergy symptoms (sneezing, itchy nose/throat, watery eyes) and hives without causing sedation.
safetyGuide: Take with water. Do not take with fruit juices (such as grapefruit, orange, or apple juice) or aluminum/magnesium antacids as they reduce drug absorption.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Use during pregnancy only if specifically prescribed by a physician.
childrenWarning: Use pediatric suspension for children aged 2-11 years as prescribed by a pediatrician.
emergencyWarning: Seek medical help if signs of severe hypersensitivity (rash, throat tightness) occur.
storage: Store between 20°C and 25°C protected from moisture.

name: Desloratadine
commonUses: Relief of nasal and non-nasal symptoms of allergic rhinitis, skin itching, and relief of pruritus in chronic urticaria.
safetyGuide: Take once daily with or without food. Non-drowsy formulation suitable for daytime use.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Consult a registered doctor before taking during pregnancy or while nursing.
childrenWarning: Use pediatric syrup under doctor guidance for children over 6 months.
emergencyWarning: Seek prompt medical care if experiencing severe skin eruptions, palpitations, or shortness of breath.
storage: Store below 30°C in moisture-resistant blisters.

name: Chlorpheniramine Maleate
commonUses: Relief of acute allergic reactions, cold symptoms, hay fever, insect bites, and allergic skin itching.
safetyGuide: Causes noticeable drowsiness. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or consuming alcohol while taking this medicine.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Consult a physician before taking. May reduce milk supply during lactation.
childrenWarning: Do not give to children under 2 years without direct pediatric prescription due to sedation risks.
emergencyWarning: Seek urgent medical help for overdose symptoms such as extreme sleepiness, seizures, or hallucinations.
storage: Store below 25°C protected from light.

name: Bilastine
commonUses: Treatment of allergic rhinoconjunctivitis (seasonal and perennial) and urticaria in adults and adolescents.
safetyGuide: MUST be taken with water on an empty stomach (1 hour before or 2 hours after food or fruit juices) for proper absorption.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Should be avoided during pregnancy and lactation unless considered essential by a physician.
childrenWarning: Use pediatric orodispersible formulation for children aged 6 to 11 years as prescribed.
emergencyWarning: Seek emergency attention if severe hypersensitivity or breathing distress occurs.
storage: Store below 30°C in original packaging.

name: Phenylephrine + Paracetamol + CPM
commonUses: Multi-symptom relief from viral common cold, fever, blocked nose, sneezing, headache, and body aches.
safetyGuide: Do NOT combine with other paracetamol products. Patients with high blood pressure, heart disease, or hyperthyroidism should consult a doctor before use.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Avoid during pregnancy due to vasoconstrictive effects of phenylephrine unless prescribed by a doctor.
childrenWarning: Not recommended for children under 6 years without direct pediatric guidance.
emergencyWarning: Seek medical help for rapid heart rate, severe dizziness, insomnia, or extreme hypertension.
storage: Store below 25°C in a cool dry area.

name: Amoxicillin
commonUses: Treats bacterial infections of the chest, throat, middle ear, sinuses, urinary tract, and dental tissues.
safetyGuide: Do not use antibiotics without a prescription from a registered physician. Complete the entire prescribed course even if symptoms improve quickly to prevent antimicrobial resistance.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Commonly prescribed during pregnancy when bacterial infection is confirmed and indicated by a physician.
childrenWarning: Pediatric suspension must be reconstituted with boiled and cooled water, stored in a refrigerator, and discarded after 7-10 days. Always use calibrated measuring syringe.
emergencyWarning: Seek immediate emergency hospital care for severe allergic reactions (anaphylaxis: facial swelling, wheezing, hives) or persistent bloody watery diarrhea.
storage: Store dry capsules below 25°C. Keep reconstituted oral suspension refrigerated (2-8°C).

name: Amoxicillin + Clavulanic Acid
commonUses: Treats resistant bacterial infections of the respiratory tract, sinusitis, otitis media, skin/soft tissue, and recurrent urinary infections.
safetyGuide: Do not use antibiotics without a prescription from a registered physician. Take at the start of a meal to optimize absorption and minimize gastrointestinal upset.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Can be used during pregnancy and lactation when clearly indicated and prescribed by an obstetrician.
childrenWarning: Follow precise pediatric dosing per body weight. Reconstituted suspension must be kept in the refrigerator and used within 7 days.
emergencyWarning: Seek emergency medical attention if severe watery diarrhea, jaundice (yellow skin/eyes), or breathing difficulty occurs.
storage: Store dry tablets below 25°C in moisture-proof packaging.

name: Azithromycin
commonUses: Treats bacterial infections of the chest (atypical pneumonia, bronchitis), throat, sinuses, skin, and sexually transmitted infections.
safetyGuide: Do not use antibiotics without a prescription from a registered physician. Take 1 hour before or 2 hours after meals. Do not take antacids containing aluminum or magnesium simultaneously.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Prescribed during pregnancy only when bacterial infection is confirmed and considered necessary by a physician.
childrenWarning: Pediatric dry syrup must be reconstituted accurately and administered with a medicine syringe.
emergencyWarning: Seek immediate emergency help if heart palpitations, severe dizziness, or severe watery diarrhea develop.
storage: Store below 30°C in dry conditions.

name: Cefixime
commonUses: Treats enteric fever (typhoid), urinary tract infections, acute otitis media, pharyngitis, and bronchitis.
safetyGuide: Do not use antibiotics without a prescription from a registered physician. May be taken with or without food. Complete the full prescribed course.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed and advised by a registered doctor.
childrenWarning: Safe in children over 6 months under pediatric prescription. Use reconstituted suspension within 14 days at room temperature or refrigerated.
emergencyWarning: Seek immediate emergency care for severe skin blisters, fever recurrence, or severe watery colitis.
storage: Store dry powder/capsules below 25°C protected from moisture.

name: Cephalexin
commonUses: Treats bacterial skin infections (cellulitis, impetigo), bone infections, strep throat, and uncomplicated urinary infections.
safetyGuide: Do not use antibiotics without a prescription from a registered physician. Take with a full glass of water. Space doses evenly throughout the 24-hour period.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Widely used during pregnancy when prescribed by a doctor for susceptible bacterial infections.
childrenWarning: Pediatric suspension must be refrigerated after reconstitution and shaken well before each dose.
emergencyWarning: Discontinue and seek immediate medical help if allergic rash, facial swelling, or severe diarrhea occurs.
storage: Store below 25°C in a dry place.

name: Doxycycline
commonUses: Treats acne vulgaris, respiratory infections, scrub typhus, cholera, chlamydia, and malaria prophylaxis.
safetyGuide: Do not use antibiotics without a prescription from a registered physician. Take with a full glass of water while sitting or standing upright. Do NOT lie down for at least 30 minutes to prevent esophageal ulceration. Avoid direct sun exposure (photosensitivity).
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED in the second and third trimesters of pregnancy due to risk of permanent tooth discoloration and impaired fetal bone growth.
childrenWarning: STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED in children under 8 years of age due to permanent yellow-gray-brown discoloration of developing teeth.
emergencyWarning: Seek immediate medical care for severe chest pain upon swallowing, intracranial hypertension (severe headache, blurred vision), or severe skin peeling.
storage: Store below 25°C protected from light and moisture.

name: Metronidazole
commonUses: Treats anaerobic bacterial infections, amoebic dysentery, giardiasis, trichomoniasis, and dental infections.
safetyGuide: Do not use antibiotics without a prescription from a registered physician. Take with or after meals. ABSOLUTELY AVOID ALCOHOL during treatment and for 48 hours after stopping to prevent severe disulfiram-like reactions (vomiting, flushing, palpitations).
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Avoid in the first trimester of pregnancy. Use in later pregnancy only if specifically prescribed by a physician.
childrenWarning: Administer pediatric suspension with accurate measuring spoon as directed by a pediatrician.
emergencyWarning: Seek emergency medical attention if numbness/tingling in hands/feet, seizures, or unsteady gait occurs.
storage: Store below 25°C protected from light.

name: Nitrofurantoin
commonUses: Specific first-line treatment and prevention of acute uncomplicated urinary tract infections (cystitis).
safetyGuide: Do not use antibiotics without a prescription from a registered physician. Must be taken with food or milk to enhance absorption and reduce stomach upset. May turn urine harmlessly dark yellow/brownish.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Contraindicated at term (38-42 weeks of pregnancy) and during labor/delivery due to risk of hemolytic anemia in the newborn.
childrenWarning: Contraindicated in infants under 1 month of age. Pediatric dosage must be calculated by a doctor.
emergencyWarning: Seek urgent medical attention if you experience sudden cough, shortness of breath, fever (pulmonary reaction), or peripheral numbness.
storage: Store below 25°C protected from light.

name: Ciprofloxacin
commonUses: Treats severe bacterial infections of the urinary tract, gastrointestinal tract (infectious diarrhea), bones, joints, and skin.
safetyGuide: Do not use antibiotics without a prescription from a registered physician. Drink plenty of water to prevent crystalluria. Do not take with dairy products alone or antacids containing calcium, iron, or zinc.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Generally avoided during pregnancy and breastfeeding unless no alternative exists and prescribed by a specialist.
childrenWarning: Generally restricted in children and growing adolescents due to potential risk of arthropathy/cartilage toxicity, except for specific indicated infections.
emergencyWarning: Stop taking and seek immediate emergency care if you feel sudden tendon pain/swelling (especially Achilles tendon), numbness, or severe confusion.
storage: Store below 30°C in moisture-resistant packaging.

name: Levofloxacin
commonUses: Treats complex respiratory tract infections (pneumonia, acute sinusitis), complicated urinary infections, and pyelonephritis.
safetyGuide: Do not use antibiotics without a prescription from a registered physician. Maintain adequate daily hydration. Space iron, calcium, and antacids by at least 2 hours.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Contraindicated during pregnancy and lactation due to risks of cartilage damage in developing joints.
childrenWarning: Not recommended in pediatric patients under 18 years unless under specialized pediatric infectious disease protocol.
emergencyWarning: Seek emergency medical help immediately if experiencing tendon pain, heart palpitations, or severe nerve sensations.
storage: Store below 25°C in original packaging protected from light.

name: Salbutamol (Albuterol)
commonUses: Rapid relief of bronchospasm in bronchial asthma, chronic bronchitis, wheezing, and COPD flare-ups.
safetyGuide: Inhale through a spacer device for better lung delivery. Using rescue inhaler more than twice a week indicates uncontrolled asthma requiring preventive controller therapy.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Commonly used for acute asthma during pregnancy under doctor guidance; maternal hypoxia poses a greater risk to the fetus than proper inhaler use.
childrenWarning: Young children should always use a pediatric spacer mask for metered-dose inhalers.
emergencyWarning: Seek immediate emergency hospital care if wheezing does not improve within 10 minutes after rescue puffs, or if user is struggling to speak or turn pale/blue.
storage: Store inhaler below 30°C away from direct sunlight and puncture risks.

name: Montelukast
commonUses: Chronic controller for long-term asthma prevention and relief of seasonal/perennial allergic rhinitis.
safetyGuide: Take once daily in the evening. NOT for treating acute sudden asthma attacks (use fast-acting bronchodilator inhalers for attacks).
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Consult your physician before taking during pregnancy or breastfeeding.
childrenWarning: Chewable tablets (4mg/5mg) and oral granules are formulated for children under pediatric prescription.
emergencyWarning: Discontinue and contact a doctor if experiencing significant neuropsychiatric changes (severe mood swings, depression, vivid nightmares).
storage: Store below 30°C in original moisture-resistant blister pack.

name: Ipratropium Bromide
commonUses: Maintenance bronchodilator therapy for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), emphysema, and acute severe asthma in combination with beta-agonists.
safetyGuide: Inhale as prescribed. Avoid spraying into eyes (especially in patients with narrow-angle glaucoma) to prevent increased ocular pressure.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Consult a physician before use during pregnancy or lactation.
childrenWarning: Pediatric nebulizer solutions should be administered under direct healthcare supervision.
emergencyWarning: Seek urgent medical attention if sudden paradoxical bronchospasm, blurred vision, or eye pain occurs.
storage: Store below 25°C away from direct heat.

name: Budesonide + Formoterol
commonUses: Daily maintenance controller and anti-inflammatory reliever for persistent asthma and severe COPD.
safetyGuide: Always rinse mouth with water and spit it out after each inhalation to prevent oral fungal thrush (candida) and hoarseness.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Inhaled budesonide has extensive safety data in pregnancy for maintaining asthma control; use under specialist guidance.
childrenWarning: Prescribed for children aged 6 years and older with spacer under pediatric pulmonology supervision.
emergencyWarning: Seek emergency care if sudden worsening of breathing occurs immediately following dose administration.
storage: Store below 30°C in a dry place with inhaler cover attached.

name: Fluticasone + Salmeterol
commonUses: Regular daily maintenance treatment for persistent asthma and reducing exacerbations in COPD.
safetyGuide: Must be used regularly every day as prescribed, not just during symptoms. Rinse and gargle with water after each use.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies potential fetal risk, under doctor supervision.
childrenWarning: Pediatric doses should be monitored regularly for growth velocity by a pediatrician.
emergencyWarning: Seek immediate emergency help if experiencing severe palpitations, chest pain, or sudden severe wheezing.
storage: Store below 30°C away from direct heat and sunlight.

name: Dextromethorphan
commonUses: Temporary relief of dry, hacking, non-productive cough caused by minor throat and bronchial irritation.
safetyGuide: Do NOT use for productive, phlegm-producing chest coughs. Do not take if you are taking MAO inhibitors or SSRI antidepressants.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Consult a healthcare professional before taking during pregnancy or while breastfeeding.
childrenWarning: Not recommended for children under 4 years of age without explicit pediatric prescription.
emergencyWarning: Seek emergency care for accidental overdose, extreme drowsiness, hallucinations, or slow breathing.
storage: Store at room temperature below 25°C.

name: Guaifenesin
commonUses: Helps loosen phlegm (mucus) and thin bronchial secretions to make productive coughs more clearing.
safetyGuide: Drink plenty of warm fluids and water while taking this medication to assist in thinning chest mucus.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Consult your physician before taking during pregnancy or lactation.
childrenWarning: Use only child-specific formulations with measured dosing cups for pediatric age groups.
emergencyWarning: Consult a doctor if cough lasts longer than 7 days, recurs, or is accompanied by high fever and rash.
storage: Store in a dry location below 30°C.

name: Ambroxol
commonUses: Secretolytic therapy in acute and chronic bronchopulmonary diseases associated with abnormal mucus secretion and impaired mucus transport.
safetyGuide: Take after meals with water. Staying well-hydrated enhances the mucolytic effect.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Avoid in the first trimester of pregnancy unless specifically prescribed by a physician.
childrenWarning: Pediatric syrup should be measured accurately and given according to age guidelines.
emergencyWarning: Discontinue and seek medical help if severe skin or mucous membrane lesions develop.
storage: Store below 25°C protected from light.

name: Fluconazole
commonUses: Treats fungal infections including oral thrush, vaginal candidiasis, esophageal candidiasis, and systemic fungal infections.
safetyGuide: Can be taken with or without food. Single-dose oral therapy is common for vaginal yeast infections; longer courses require physician oversight.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: High-dose or long-term fluconazole is CONTRAINDICATED in pregnancy due to risk of birth defects. Consult a doctor.
childrenWarning: Pediatric dosing must be calculated strictly according to body weight by a pediatrician.
emergencyWarning: Seek emergency medical evaluation for severe abdominal pain, persistent nausea, jaundice, or dark urine (signs of liver toxicity).
storage: Store below 30°C in a dry location.

name: Itraconazole
commonUses: Treats fungal nail infections (onychomycosis), systemic aspergillosis, blastomycosis, and histoplasmosis.
safetyGuide: Take immediately after a full meal to maximize absorption. Avoid concurrent antacids as stomach acid is required for dissolution.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Contraindicated in pregnancy and women planning pregnancy due to fetal risk.
childrenWarning: Not recommended in children unless no suitable alternative antifungal exists and prescribed by a specialist.
emergencyWarning: Seek immediate medical attention for shortness of breath, unexplained swelling (signs of heart failure), or liver discomfort.
storage: Store below 25°C protected from moisture and light.

name: Terbinafine
commonUses: Treats fungal infections of the toenails/fingernails, athlete's foot (tinea pedis), ringworm (tinea corporis), and jock itch (tinea cruris).
safetyGuide: Oral tablets require several weeks of continuous therapy for fungal nail clearance. Topical cream is applied once or twice daily to cleaned and dried affected skin.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Oral terbinafine should not be started during pregnancy or lactation unless essential.
childrenWarning: Topical cream suitable for older children; oral therapy strictly managed by pediatric dermatology.
emergencyWarning: Discontinue immediately and seek medical help for persistent taste disturbance, severe depression, or yellowing of eyes.
storage: Store below 30°C in a dry place.

name: Clotrimazole
commonUses: Topical treatment for athlete's foot, jock itch, cutaneous candidiasis, ringworm, and vaginal yeast infections.
safetyGuide: For external or vaginal use only. Apply a thin layer to the affected area and rub in gently. Continue for at least 1-2 weeks after symptoms disappear to prevent recurrence.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Topical and vaginal clotrimazole are generally considered safe during pregnancy under healthcare advice.
childrenWarning: Safe for children when applied topically for diaper fungal rash under pediatric direction.
emergencyWarning: Discontinue use if severe local skin irritation, blistering, or redness occurs.
storage: Store below 25°C. Do not freeze.

name: Ketoconazole
commonUses: Treatment and prevention of dandruff, seborrheic dermatitis, and pityriasis versicolor (tinea versicolor).
safetyGuide: Apply shampoo to wet hair/scalp, leave on for 3 to 5 minutes before rinsing thoroughly. Oral ketoconazole has high liver toxicity risks and is reserved for specific hospital use.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Topical shampoo has minimal systemic absorption and may be used during pregnancy if approved by a doctor.
childrenWarning: Safety and efficacy of shampoo in children under 12 years have not been established.
emergencyWarning: Avoid contact with eyes. Rinse thoroughly with water if accidental eye contact occurs.
storage: Store below 25°C in original bottle.

name: Acyclovir
commonUses: Treatment of herpes simplex virus infections (cold sores, genital herpes), herpes zoster (shingles), and chickenpox (varicella).
safetyGuide: Start treatment as early as possible after the onset of signs or symptoms (e.g. within 48-72 hours of rash). Maintain good hydration to protect kidney function.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Can be used during pregnancy and lactation when indicated and prescribed by a doctor for maternal infection.
childrenWarning: Weight-based pediatric dosing is used for chickenpox or pediatric herpes under pediatric supervision.
emergencyWarning: Seek medical attention if experiencing sudden confusion, decreased urination, or extreme fatigue.
storage: Store below 25°C in a dry place.

name: Valacyclovir
commonUses: Treatment of herpes zoster (shingles), cold sores, and suppression of recurrent genital herpes with convenient dosing.
safetyGuide: Drink plenty of fluids while taking valacyclovir. Complete the full course prescribed by your physician.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed and approved by a physician.
childrenWarning: Not routinely indicated for young children without specialist prescription.
emergencyWarning: Seek emergency medical care if experiencing confusion, hallucinations, or signs of renal failure.
storage: Store below 30°C in original packaging.

name: Oseltamivir
commonUses: Treatment and post-exposure prophylaxis of acute uncomplicated influenza A and B (flu) infection.
safetyGuide: Most effective when initiated within 48 hours of onset of flu symptoms (fever, chills, body ache). Take with food to reduce nausea.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Recommended for pregnant women with confirmed or suspected influenza due to high risk of severe viral complications.
childrenWarning: Pediatric oral suspension is approved for infants and children; dosing strictly calculated by pediatrician.
emergencyWarning: Seek medical attention if severe abnormal behavior, delirium, or severe skin rash develops.
storage: Store capsules below 25°C. Reconstituted suspension should be stored refrigerated (2-8°C) and used within 10 days.

name: Albendazole
commonUses: Treatment of single or mixed intestinal parasite infections (roundworm, pinworm, hookworm, whipworm, tapeworm) and hydatid disease.
safetyGuide: Tablets should be crushed or chewed before swallowing with water. For pinworm infection, a second dose after 2 weeks is often recommended to prevent re-infection.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED during the first trimester of pregnancy. Avoid in women planning to conceive.
childrenWarning: Safe in children aged 1-2 years at reduced dose and full dose for children >2 years as per national deworming guidelines.
emergencyWarning: Seek medical advice if high fever, severe headache, or abdominal pain occurs.
storage: Store below 30°C protected from light.

name: Mebendazole
commonUses: Treatment of pinworm (enterobiasis), roundworm (ascariasis), hookworm, and whipworm infections.
safetyGuide: Chew tablets completely before swallowing. Treat all household members simultaneously if treating pinworms to prevent transmission.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Avoid during the first trimester of pregnancy. Consult a doctor during lactation.
childrenWarning: Not recommended for children under 2 years of age unless specifically prescribed by a pediatrician.
emergencyWarning: Seek medical care if allergic swelling or severe abdominal cramping develops.
storage: Store below 25°C in a dry place.

name: Ivermectin
commonUses: Treatment of crusted/resistant scabies, cutaneous larva migrans, strongyloidiasis, and onchocerciasis.
safetyGuide: Take as a single dose with water on an empty stomach (at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after a meal). Follow strict personal hygiene and wash bedding to eradicate scabies.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Contraindicated during pregnancy unless benefits clearly outweigh risks under specialist supervision.
childrenWarning: Not recommended for children weighing less than 15 kg.
emergencyWarning: Seek immediate hospital evaluation if experiencing severe dizziness, blurred vision, loss of balance, or seizures.
storage: Store below 30°C in moisture-resistant blisters.

name: Amlodipine
commonUses: First-line treatment for essential hypertension (high blood pressure) and chronic stable angina.
safetyGuide: Take once daily at the same time each day with or without food. Mild ankle swelling (peripheral edema) is a known side effect; report significant swelling to your physician. Do not stop abruptly.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Consult a cardiologist/obstetrician; usually substituted with safer anti-hypertensive alternatives during pregnancy.
childrenWarning: Pediatric use strictly limited to specialist pediatric nephrology/cardiology protocols.
emergencyWarning: Seek emergency medical care for severe dizziness, fainting, sudden chest pain, or irregular heartbeat.
storage: Store below 25°C protected from light and moisture.

name: Losartan
commonUses: Treatment of hypertension, diabetic nephropathy in type 2 diabetes, and stroke risk reduction.
safetyGuide: Take with or without food. Regularly monitor kidney function (creatinine) and potassium levels. Do not use salt substitutes containing potassium without physician approval.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED in pregnancy (second and third trimesters) due to severe fetal renal failure and death.
childrenWarning: Pediatric use requires specific specialist prescription with careful blood pressure monitoring.
emergencyWarning: Seek urgent emergency help if you experience swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or difficulty breathing (angioedema).
storage: Store in a dry place below 30°C.

name: Telmisartan
commonUses: 24-hour control of essential hypertension and reduction of cardiovascular morbidity in high-risk patients.
safetyGuide: Long half-life provides sustained blood pressure control. Take once daily with water. Keep in original moisture-barrier blister until immediately before consumption.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED during pregnancy due to potential fetal toxicity.
childrenWarning: Safety and efficacy not established in children under 18 years.
emergencyWarning: Seek emergency help for severe hypotension (fainting), hyperkalemia, or angioedema.
storage: Store below 30°C in original blister pack to protect from atmospheric moisture.

name: Bisoprolol
commonUses: Treatment of chronic stable heart failure, hypertension, and angina pectoris.
safetyGuide: Take in the morning with or without breakfast. NEVER stop taking bisoprolol abruptly as this can precipitate severe rebound hypertension or cardiac ischemia.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: May reduce placental perfusion; use during pregnancy only if strictly monitored and prescribed by a cardiologist.
childrenWarning: Not recommended for pediatric use.
emergencyWarning: Seek emergency medical care for very slow heart rate (<45 bpm), severe dizziness, or worsening shortness of breath.
storage: Store below 25°C in a dry area.

name: Atenolol
commonUses: Management of hypertension, long-term prophylaxis of angina, and cardiac arrhythmias.
safetyGuide: Take at the same time each day. Check your pulse regularly. Do not discontinue without tapering under doctor supervision.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Associated with fetal growth restriction; avoid in pregnancy unless no alternative exists.
childrenWarning: Pediatric use strictly supervised by pediatric cardiology specialists.
emergencyWarning: Seek urgent medical attention for severe bradycardia, fainting, or sudden wheezing.
storage: Store below 25°C protected from light.

name: Enalapril
commonUses: Treatment of hypertension, symptomatic heart failure, and prevention of coronary ischemia.
safetyGuide: Take once or twice daily. A persistent dry cough may occur in some patients; report this to your doctor for potential medication adjustment.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED in pregnancy due to severe risks of fetal injury and oligohydramnios.
childrenWarning: Use in children with hypertension requires careful specialist titration.
emergencyWarning: Seek immediate emergency help if swelling of the lips, tongue, or throat (angioedema) occurs.
storage: Store below 30°C protected from moisture.

name: Hydrochlorothiazide
commonUses: Treatment of edema associated with heart failure and combination therapy for essential hypertension.
safetyGuide: Best taken in the morning to prevent nighttime urination. Monitor electrolytes (potassium, sodium) periodically. Protect skin from excessive sun exposure.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Avoid in pregnancy due to risk of decreased placental perfusion unless specifically indicated for maternal edema.
childrenWarning: Pediatric dosing strictly guided by pediatric nephrology.
emergencyWarning: Seek medical evaluation for muscle cramps, extreme thirst, confusion, or severe electrolyte imbalance.
storage: Store below 25°C in a dry place.

name: Glyceryl Trinitrate (Nitroglycerin)
commonUses: Rapid acute relief and prevention of angina pectoris (chest pain) attacks.
safetyGuide: Sublingual tablets/spray must be placed under the tongue at the onset of an angina attack while sitting down (to prevent falls from dizziness). STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED with phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors (e.g. Sildenafil, Tadalafil) due to fatal hypotension risks.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Use in pregnancy only if clearly needed under specialist cardiology supervision.
childrenWarning: Not indicated for pediatric use.
emergencyWarning: If chest pain is NOT relieved after 1 sublingual dose (or persists after 5 minutes), immediately call emergency medical services (999/hospital ambulance) for suspected myocardial infarction.
storage: Store in original tightly closed glass bottle below 25°C away from heat and light.

name: Atorvastatin
commonUses: Lowers LDL cholesterol, triglycerides, and reduces the risk of heart attacks, stroke, and arterial disease.
safetyGuide: Take once daily in the evening or morning with or without food. Avoid excessive consumption of grapefruit juice. Maintain a heart-healthy diet.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED during pregnancy and breastfeeding due to potential harm to fetal lipid development.
childrenWarning: Pediatric use strictly limited to specialized pediatric lipid clinics for familial hypercholesterolemia.
emergencyWarning: Seek prompt medical care if you experience unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness accompanied by dark brown urine (rhabdomyolysis).
storage: Store below 25°C protected from moisture.

name: Rosuvastatin
commonUses: Primary prevention of cardiovascular events and management of severe primary hyperlipidemia and mixed dyslipidemia.
safetyGuide: Take once daily at any time of day with or without food. Space antacids by at least 2 hours. Do not discontinue without consulting your physician.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED in pregnancy and lactation.
childrenWarning: Prescribed only by pediatric lipid specialists for children >6 years with severe genetic lipid disorders.
emergencyWarning: Contact a doctor immediately if severe muscle cramps, extreme fatigue, or yellowing of the eyes occurs.
storage: Store below 30°C in original packaging.

name: Fenofibrate
commonUses: Reduction of severely elevated blood triglycerides (hypertriglyceridemia) to reduce the risk of pancreatitis.
safetyGuide: Take with meals to optimize absorption. Periodic monitoring of liver enzymes and renal function is required during therapy.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Avoid during pregnancy and breastfeeding unless considered essential by a physician.
childrenWarning: Safety and efficacy in children have not been established.
emergencyWarning: Seek medical evaluation for severe right upper abdominal pain (gallstones) or muscle soreness.
storage: Store below 25°C in a dry place.

name: Metformin
commonUses: First-line oral treatment for Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and management of insulin resistance in PCOS.
safetyGuide: ALWAYS take with or immediately after meals to reduce stomach upset and nausea. Extended-release (XR) tablets must be swallowed whole without chewing. Temporarily stop before iodinated CT contrast procedures.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Widely used under obstetric guidance for gestational diabetes and PCOS.
childrenWarning: Approved for children aged 10 years and older with type 2 diabetes under pediatric endocrinologist direction.
emergencyWarning: Seek immediate emergency hospital care for severe weakness, rapid deep breathing, hypothermia, or severe stomach pain (signs of lactic acidosis).
storage: Store below 25°C in a dry place.

name: Gliclazide
commonUses: Management of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus in adults when dietary measures and exercise alone are insufficient.
safetyGuide: Take strictly with breakfast. Never skip a meal after taking gliclazide to prevent hypoglycemia (dangerously low blood sugar). Always carry glucose or sweet candy.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Contraindicated in pregnancy; insulin is the standard treatment during pregnancy.
childrenWarning: Not indicated for pediatric use.
emergencyWarning: Treat symptoms of low blood sugar (sweating, shaking, dizziness, confusion) immediately with fast-acting sugar. Seek emergency care if patient becomes unconscious.
storage: Store below 30°C away from moisture.

name: Glimepiride
commonUses: Blood glucose control in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus as monotherapy or combined with metformin.
safetyGuide: Take with breakfast or the first main meal. Ensure regular meals throughout the day to avoid hypoglycemia.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Contraindicated in pregnancy and nursing mothers.
childrenWarning: Not recommended in children.
emergencyWarning: Emergency treatment required for severe hypoglycemia or allergic skin reactions.
storage: Store below 25°C in original packaging.

name: Sitagliptin
commonUses: Improves glycemic control in adults with Type 2 Diabetes by enhancing active incretin hormone levels.
safetyGuide: Take once daily with or without food. Low risk of hypoglycemia when used as monotherapy. Dose adjustment needed in renal impairment.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed and approved by a diabetes specialist.
childrenWarning: Safety and efficacy not established in pediatric patients.
emergencyWarning: Seek immediate medical attention for persistent severe abdominal pain radiating to the back (signs of pancreatitis).
storage: Store below 25°C in a dry location.

name: Linagliptin
commonUses: Glycemic control in Type 2 Diabetes, particularly advantageous in patients with renal impairment (no dose adjustment required).
safetyGuide: Take once daily with or without food. Safe across all stages of kidney function.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Consult your doctor before use during pregnancy or lactation.
childrenWarning: Not approved for pediatric patients.
emergencyWarning: Seek emergency medical help if experiencing severe joint pain, skin blisters, or severe abdominal pain.
storage: Store below 30°C protected from moisture.

name: Empagliflozin
commonUses: Type 2 Diabetes management, reducing cardiovascular death risk, and treating chronic heart failure and chronic kidney disease.
safetyGuide: Take once daily in the morning with or without food. Drink plenty of water throughout the day. Maintain meticulous genital hygiene to prevent fungal urinary tract infections.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Contraindicated in the second and third trimesters of pregnancy and while breastfeeding.
childrenWarning: Not indicated for pediatric use.
emergencyWarning: Seek emergency medical care immediately for severe nausea, confusion, rapid breathing, and malaise even with normal blood sugar levels (Euglycemic Diabetic Ketoacidosis).
storage: Store below 25°C in original packaging.

name: Levothyroxine
commonUses: Replacement therapy for primary, secondary, and tertiary hypothyroidism, and suppression of thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) in goiter.
safetyGuide: MUST be taken on an empty stomach first thing in the morning with a full glass of water, at least 30 to 60 minutes BEFORE breakfast. Separate calcium, iron, or antacids by at least 4 hours.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: ESSENTIAL during pregnancy for fetal neurological development. Thyroid requirements often increase during pregnancy; regular TSH blood tests are required.
childrenWarning: Congenital hypothyroidism requires urgent lifelong replacement under pediatric endocrinologist supervision.
emergencyWarning: Seek prompt medical care for chest pain, rapid or irregular heartbeat, tremors, or extreme heat intolerance (signs of excessive dose).
storage: Store below 25°C protected from light and moisture.

name: Carbimazole
commonUses: Management of hyperthyroidism (Graves' disease), preparation for thyroidectomy, and radioiodine therapy.
safetyGuide: Take regularly as prescribed. Blood cell counts (CBC) and liver tests must be monitored regularly.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Use lowest effective dose during pregnancy under endocrinology supervision (Propylthiouracil is often preferred in first trimester).
childrenWarning: Pediatric hyperthyroidism requires specialist pediatric endocrinology monitoring.
emergencyWarning: STOP taking immediately and see a doctor urgently if you develop a sore throat, mouth ulcers, or high fever (critical sign of agranulocytosis/low white blood cells).
storage: Store below 25°C in a dry place.

name: Norethisterone
commonUses: Treatment of dysfunctional uterine bleeding, painful periods (dysmenorrhea), endometriosis, and temporary postponement of menstruation.
safetyGuide: Take exactly as directed by your gynecologist. For delaying periods, start 3 days before expected menses and continue for no longer than directed.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED in known or suspected pregnancy.
childrenWarning: Not indicated for pre-pubertal children.
emergencyWarning: Seek emergency medical help for signs of thromboembolism: sudden severe calf pain, chest pain, or sudden severe headache.
storage: Store below 25°C protected from light.

name: Prednisolone
commonUses: Powerful anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive treatment for acute asthma attacks, allergic crises, autoimmune diseases, and nephrotic syndrome.
safetyGuide: Take in the morning with or immediately after breakfast to match natural cortisol rhythms and protect stomach. NEVER stop long-term therapy suddenly; doses must be tapered gradually under physician guidance.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Use during pregnancy only when indicated and prescribed by a specialist. Monitor newborn for adrenal insufficiency if high doses were used.
childrenWarning: Pediatric short courses are common for croup or asthma flare-ups; prolonged use requires close pediatric growth monitoring.
emergencyWarning: Seek immediate emergency help for signs of acute infection, severe stomach ulcer pain, mental status changes, or adrenal crisis.
storage: Store below 25°C protected from light and moisture.

name: Dexamethasone
commonUses: Treatment of severe allergic states, cerebral edema, severe respiratory distress, croup, and acute inflammatory emergencies.
safetyGuide: Take with meals. High potency steroid; strictly adhere to physician prescribed duration and tapering protocol.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Crosses the placenta; used specifically in obstetric emergencies for fetal lung maturation under specialist supervision.
childrenWarning: Used in single or short doses for pediatric croup under strict medical supervision.
emergencyWarning: Seek emergency care for severe mood disturbances, acute visual changes, or signs of severe systemic infection.
storage: Store below 25°C in dry conditions.

name: Hydrocortisone
commonUses: Replacement therapy in primary/secondary adrenocortical insufficiency (Addison's disease) and emergency management of acute adrenal crisis.
safetyGuide: Take with meals. Patients with adrenal insufficiency should wear medical alert identification and increase dose during acute illness/surgery under physician direction.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Essential to maintain physiological hormone levels during pregnancy under endocrinologist care.
childrenWarning: Pediatric replacement therapy requires precise body surface area dosing by a pediatric endocrinologist.
emergencyWarning: Seek immediate emergency hospital care for signs of acute adrenal crisis (severe vomiting, dehydration, profound hypotension, confusion).
storage: Store below 25°C protected from moisture.

name: Povidone Iodine
commonUses: Disinfection of minor wounds, cuts, abrasions, burns, and surgical skin preparation.
safetyGuide: For external topical use only. Clean the wound area and apply antiseptic solution or ointment directly. Allow to dry. Do NOT use if allergic to iodine.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Avoid prolonged application over large body surface areas during pregnancy or breastfeeding due to iodine absorption.
childrenWarning: Avoid prolonged use in premature infants and neonates due to risk of thyroid dysfunction.
emergencyWarning: Seek emergency care if accidental ingestion occurs or if deep animal bites/puncture wounds are present.
storage: Store below 25°C protected from light. Keep cap tightly closed.

name: Silver Sulfadiazine
commonUses: Prevention and treatment of bacterial wound sepsis in second- and third-degree thermal burns and skin graft donor sites.
safetyGuide: Apply using sterile gloved hands as a 1-2 mm layer over cleaned and debrided burn areas once or twice daily.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: CONTRAINDICATED in late pregnancy approaching term and during nursing of infants under 2 months due to risk of kernicterus.
childrenWarning: Contraindicated in premature infants and neonates under 2 months of age.
emergencyWarning: Seek urgent hospital burn unit care for extensive, deep, or facial burns.
storage: Store below 25°C. Do not freeze.

name: Fusidic Acid
commonUses: Topical treatment of bacterial skin infections such as impetigo, folliculitis, infected cuts, and infected eczema.
safetyGuide: Apply a thin layer to the affected area 2 to 3 times daily for 7 to 10 days. Avoid contact with eyes. Do not overuse topicals to prevent resistant strains.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Topical formulation is considered safe during pregnancy and lactation; avoid applying directly on nipples before breastfeeding.
childrenWarning: Safe for use in children for localized skin infections under parental supervision.
emergencyWarning: Seek medical attention if localized infection spreads, worsens, or causes red streaks.
storage: Store below 25°C.

name: Calamine Lotion
commonUses: Relief of itching, discomfort, and irritation from chickenpox, sunburn, insect stings, poison ivy, and prickly heat.
safetyGuide: Shake bottle well before use. Apply to affected skin using clean cotton wool. For external use only; do not apply to open bleeding wounds or near eyes.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Safe for external use during pregnancy and lactation.
childrenWarning: Gentle and safe for children and toddlers experiencing viral rashes or insect bites.
emergencyWarning: Consult a doctor if rash spreads rapidly, becomes infected, or is accompanied by high fever.
storage: Store below 30°C. Keep bottle tightly closed.

name: Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS)
genericName: Sodium Chloride, Potassium Chloride, Sodium Citrate, Anhydrous Glucose (WHO Low-Osmolarity Formula)
commonUses: Essential fluid and electrolyte replacement for acute diarrhea, vomiting, cholera, food poisoning, heat exhaustion, and dehydration.
safetyGuide: Dissolve 1 standard sachet in EXACTLY the specified volume of clean, cool drinking water (e.g. exactly 500 ml for a 500 ml sachet). Give small, frequent sips. Discard any reconstituted solution remaining after 24 hours.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Completely safe and strongly recommended during pregnancy and lactation to prevent maternal dehydration.
childrenWarning: Continue breastfeeding alongside ORS. Never mix powder with milk, juice, or hot water. Always measure clean water precisely.
emergencyWarning: Seek urgent hospital emergency care if the patient is unable to drink, unusually sleepy/unresponsive, has sunken eyes, or produces no urine.
storage: Store dry sachets in a dry place at room temperature.

name: Vitamin D3 (Cholecalciferol)
commonUses: Treatment and prevention of Vitamin D deficiency, supporting calcium absorption, bone mineralization, and immune health.
safetyGuide: Best taken with a meal containing dietary fats to enhance absorption. Follow physician-prescribed frequency (e.g., daily drops or weekly/monthly high-dose capsules).
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Safe and commonly recommended during pregnancy and lactation at recommended nutritional intake levels.
childrenWarning: Pediatric drops are standard for infants to prevent rickets. Use calibrated dropper.
emergencyWarning: Seek medical evaluation for signs of hypervitaminosis D (nausea, vomiting, excessive thirst, weakness, kidney stones).
storage: Store below 25°C protected from light and heat.

name: Calcium + Vitamin D3
commonUses: Prevention and treatment of osteoporosis, osteopenia, calcium deficiency, and supporting bone density during aging and pregnancy.
safetyGuide: Take with or immediately after meals with a full glass of water. Space doses of iron supplements and thyroid medications by at least 2 to 4 hours.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Standard supportive supplement in pregnancy and lactation to support fetal skeletal growth.
childrenWarning: Use pediatric syrups for children under doctor supervision.
emergencyWarning: Consult a physician if you have a history of kidney stones (nephrolithiasis) or hypercalcemia.
storage: Store below 30°C in a dry place.

name: Vitamin B-Complex
commonUses: Treatment and prophylaxis of B-vitamin deficiencies, peripheral neuropathy, convalescence, fatigue, and mouth ulcers.
safetyGuide: Take with meals. May cause harmless bright yellow discoloration of urine due to riboflavin excretion.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Safe and beneficial at recommended dietary allowances during pregnancy and lactation.
childrenWarning: Use pediatric vitamin syrups with calibrated dosing.
emergencyWarning: Seek medical advice for unexplained allergic skin reactions or burning sensations.
storage: Store below 25°C in a cool dry area.

name: Iron + Folic Acid
commonUses: Prevention and treatment of iron deficiency anemia and neural tube defect prevention during pregnancy.
safetyGuide: Take with meals to reduce gastrointestinal discomfort. Expect harmless darkening of stools. Avoid taking with tea, coffee, or milk which inhibit iron absorption; take with vitamin C/citrus to enhance uptake.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Essential standard prenatal supplement recommended throughout pregnancy and postpartum.
childrenWarning: KEEP CAREFULLY OUT OF REACH OF CHILDREN. Accidental iron overdose in toddlers is a medical emergency.
emergencyWarning: In case of accidental acute overdose by a child, rush immediately to an emergency hospital (iron toxicity requires deferoxamine).
storage: Store below 25°C in child-resistant packaging.

name: Vitamin C (Ascorbic Acid)
commonUses: Treatment and prevention of scurvy, supporting wound healing, iron absorption, collagen synthesis, and immune defense.
safetyGuide: Chewable tablets should be chewed before swallowing. Effervescent tablets should be fully dissolved in a glass of drinking water.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Safe at recommended nutritional levels during pregnancy and breastfeeding.
childrenWarning: Safe and pleasant for children at age-appropriate dietary allowances.
emergencyWarning: Excessive intake (>2000mg/day) may cause osmotic diarrhea and increase the risk of oxalate kidney stones.
storage: Store in a tightly closed container below 25°C protected from moisture and light.

name: Zinc Sulfate
commonUses: Adjunct therapy with ORS for pediatric acute diarrhea to reduce duration and recurrence, and treatment of zinc deficiency.
safetyGuide: Take with food to minimize nausea. In pediatric diarrhea management, continue daily zinc for the full 10-14 day course even after diarrhea stops.
pregnancyBreastfeedingWarning: Safe during pregnancy and lactation within recommended daily allowances.
childrenWarning: WHO/UNICEF standard adjunct for diarrhea in infants and young children; use dispersible tablets or syrup.
emergencyWarning: Seek medical help for severe persistent vomiting or abdominal cramps.
storage: Store below 30°C in a dry place.
